competitorCoverage: Top-ranking Google articles on 'exercise for seniors' universally emphasize the 150 minutes weekly of moderate aerobic activity plus two days of strength training, per updated Physical Activity Guidelines, alongside benefits like fall prevention, muscle preservation, and chronic disease management.[1][3] They highlight low-impact options such as walking, water aerobics, yoga, and Tai Chi, with advice to start slow, consult doctors, and include balance and flexibility work.[2][4] To compete, a new article must cover these guidelines, provide beginner-friendly routines with progressions, and address common fears like injury or age barriers with evidence-based reassurances.[3][7]
